packet.headline_seed: Thousand welcome home Cape Verde footballers after stunning World Cup run
packet.description_seed: Tens of thousands of fans formed an ocean of blue outside the airport in capital city, Praia.

what: Thousand welcome home Cape Verde footballers after stunning World Cup run

clean_source_blocks.text: Tens of thousands of fans formed an ocean of blue outside the airport in capital city, Praia.

Thousands turned out to welcome the players home Cape Verde's football team have been welcomed home by tens of thousands of elated supporters following a historic run at the World Cup. The Blue Sharks flew into the capital city, Praia, on Sunday, having been knocked out of the tournament after a thrilling match against reigning champions Argentina. Jubilant fans transformed the airport's grounds into a carnival of sorts, banging drums, dancing, chanting and waving the national flag. Goalkeeper Vozinha, who drew global attention with his performances, told the BBC: "It is a very great moment for us to be here with our people. The airport grounds turned into a sea of blue on Sunday

"We wanted something bigger but we didn't go to the next stage. Now we just enjoy the moment and celebrate with our people," said Vozinha, real name Josimar José Évora Dias, while wearing a white T-shirt emblazoned with his country's name. One supporter told the BBC she attended the homecoming in order to show her gratitude to the Blue Sharks, who represented the World Cup's second-smallest nation and had never played in the tournament before, yet held their own against giants like Spain and Uruguay. Pico Lopes, 33, played a starring role in Cape Verde's World Cup matches Fans at the airport screamed Vozinha's name, as well as those of other stars, such as centre-back Pico Lopes. Amid the celebrations, the players took turns to sign fans' football tops. Fans danced and chanted as the Blue Sharks flew into Praia

They wrote one of the fairy-tale stories of this World Cup. Cape Verde remained unbeaten in the group stage, picked up three draws, and advanced to the round of 32. Even against Lionel Messi and his Argentina side, the island nation managed to score twice, and the match remained open for a long time. Many experts later called it one of the best games of the tournament. Now the team returned home and was welcomed by a huge number of fans. The airport staff was also thrilled by the boys' performance at the World Cup in the United States, Canada, and Mexico. Accordingly, there was also great interest from journalists, and after landing the players first had to give a few interviews. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. [Lähde: FOX Sports]
Cape Verde won hearts across the world with its inspiring run at the 2026 World Cup. The island country with a population of under 600,000 people — located within an archipelago off the western coast of Africa — fielded a team of players who never backed down even against the top-ranked team in the tournament.

During the group stage, they took points off previous World Cup-winning nations Spain and Uruguay, before a draw with Saudi Arabia clinched Cape Verde's spot in the knockout rounds. The magic continued, as Cape Verde went blow for blow with defending champion Argentina, matching its first goal in regulation, and another in extra time when Sidny Lopes Cabral delivered the goal of the tournament.

[Lähde: New York Post]

Cape Verde’s historic World Cup draw against Spain has turned its 40-year-old goalkeeper into one of the early breakout stories of the tournament.

Josimar José Évora Dias, known as Vozinha, produced a standout performance Monday as Cape Verde held Spain to a stunning 0-0 draw in its World Cup opener, recording seven saves.

For a nation appearing at the tournament for the first time, a point against one of world soccer’s biggest names was a landmark result.

For Vozinha, it also brought an extraordinary surge in attention.

The veteran keeper’s Instagram following climbed from roughly 46,000 before kickoff to roughly 2.4 million as of this writing, turning him from a respected international veteran into one of the tournament’s most talked-about players.

It was a performance for the ages, and Cape Verde's 40-year-old goalkeeper, Vozinha, has got the follower growth to match 🔥 pic.twitter.com/a8xIFJpBzJ

“I worked all my life for this, for this moment, for this dream,” Vozinha told Fox after the game. “A lot of generations in the past was dreaming for this.’

The rise fits into a wider World Cup trend in which lesser-known players have suddenly found themselves pushed into the spotlight through social media.

The Post previously reported on NYCFC defender Kai Trewin going viral before the tournament, while New Zealand defender Tim Payne also saw his following explode after an online push from fans.

Vozinha’s surge, though, came directly off the back of a result that will mean far more than a few extra followers.

Spain entered the match expected to start its campaign with a win, but Cape Verde frustrated the European powerhouse throughout the game. The tournament debutants stayed organized, absorbed pressure and relied on their veteran goalkeeper to help see them through.

payload.title: Kap Verden jalkapallomaajoukkue sai sankarivastaanoton Praiassa
payload.summary: Kymmenettuhannet kannattajat kokoontuivat Praian lentokentän ympärille juhlimaan Kap Verden jalkapallomaajoukkuetta historiallisen MM-turnauksen jälkeen.
payload.content:
Kymmenettuhannet kannattajat ottivat Kap Verden jalkapallomaajoukkueen vastaan pääkaupunki Praiassa sunnuntaina sen jälkeen, kun joukkueen historiallinen MM-taival oli päättynyt otteluun hallitsevaa mestaria Argentiinaa vastaan. Lentokentän ympäristö täyttyi siniseen pukeutuneista faneista, rummuista, tanssista, huudoista ja kansallislipuista.

## Lentokentästä tuli juhla-alue

Kap Verden maajoukkue, lempinimeltään Blue Sharks, palasi kotiin turnauksesta, jossa se nousi yhdeksi kisojen puhutuimmista tarinoista. Joukkue ei ollut aiemmin pelannut MM-turnauksessa, mutta eteni alkulohkosta kolmella tasapelillä 32 parhaan joukkoon.

Praiassa vastaanotto oli poikkeuksellisen lämmin. Kannattajat muuttivat lentokentän alueen juhla-alueeksi, jossa pelaajien nimiä huudettiin ja fanit yrittivät saada pelipaitoihinsa nimikirjoituksia. Erityistä huomiota sai maalivahti Vozinha, oikealta nimeltään Josimar José Évora Dias, jonka otteet turnauksessa keräsivät laajaa kiinnostusta.

Vozinha kuvaili kotiinpaluuta suureksi hetkeksi joukkueelle ja sen kannattajille. Hän sanoi joukkueen tavoitelleen vielä enemmän, mutta korosti, että nyt oli aika nauttia hetkestä ja juhlia oman kansan kanssa. Lentokentällä myös henkilökunta ja paikalle saapuneet toimittajat osoittivat kiinnostusta joukkueen esityksiin.

## Pieni maa nousi suurelle näyttämölle

Kap Verde oli turnauksen toiseksi pienin maa, mutta se pystyi haastamaan huomattavasti suurempia jalkapallomaita. Joukkue piti lähteiden mukaan pintansa muun muassa Espanjaa ja Uruguayta vastaan ja jäi turnauksessa mieleen yhtenä kisojen yllätystarinoista.

Myös ottelu Argentiinaa vastaan jäi vahvasti mieleen. Kap Verde teki Lionel Messin tähdittämää hallitsevaa mestaria vastaan kaksi maalia, ja peli pysyi pitkään avoimena. Useat asiantuntijat kuvailivat ottelua myöhemmin yhdeksi turnauksen parhaista.

Kannattajille kotiinpaluu oli ennen kaikkea kiitoksen hetki. Yksi fani kertoi tulleensa paikalle osoittaakseen arvostusta joukkueelle, joka oli vienyt saarivaltion näkyvästi maailman suurimmalle jalkapallonäyttämölle. Pelaajista myös 33-vuotias toppari Pico Lopes sai lentokentällä runsaasti huomiota kannattajilta.
summary_bullets: Kap Verden maajoukkue palasi sunnuntaina Praiaan historiallisen MM-turnauksen jälkeen.
Kymmenettuhannet kannattajat juhlivat joukkuetta lentokentän ympäristössä.
Joukkue eteni ensimmäisessä MM-turnauksessaan 32 parhaan joukkoon ja haastoi suurmaita.
